blocks.text: You can configure grouping rules to aggregate policy violations into a single violation ticket, for a focused and streamlined workflow. During the initial setup, a default rule set based on best practices is created based on the policy name and policy assignee. You can create and modify a grouping rule to align with your organization's requirements.
You can create a rule set in the following ways:

blocks.item: Create a new grouping rule set: Add a new rule set, activate, and run the rule set to reaggregate policy violations into violation tickets. Activating the new rule set deactivates the existing rule set.
Clone and edit the default rule set: Clone and edit the default rule set. Run the edited rule set to reaggregate policy violations into violation tickets based on the newly configured grouping logic.

blocks.heading: Configuring a New Grouping Rule Set

blocks.text: A grouping rule set is a collection of individual rules that group similar policy violations into violation tickets based on specific conditions. While you can create multiple rule sets within an account, only one rule set can be active at a time.
To configure a grouping rule set:

blocks.item: In the SecOps platform, click Assets in the top navigation bar.
Go to Settings > Grouping Rules.
The Grouping Rule Sets page appears.
See image.
Click New Rule Set.
The Create New Rule Set page appears.
Enter a name for the rule set.
Click New Rule.
The Create Rule page appears.
See image.
On the Create Rule page:
Name: Enter a name for the rule.
If: Define the condition that determines which policy violations the rule applies to.
Then: Select an action from the Group By drop-down menu that must be implemented when the conditions are met.
Define Violation Ticket Title By: Select a title format for the violation tickets.

Smart Text: Use a combination of free text and field names as tokens for the title. For example, you can enter the name of the team based on the business application associated with the violation ticket. To add fields as tokens, enter the field name within double curly brackets. The field's display name automatically translates to the field's system name (e.g., Application Name → application.name).

Expression: Set a violation ticket title using an expression to apply custom value transformations and standardize formats. Supported functions, operators, and references, along with examples, are displayed when clicking the Expression text box.
(Optional) Click Preview to validate the rule's logic.
Click Save.
To activate the new rule, click Save & Activate from the Save drop-down menu.
Click Save.

This saves the rule but doesn't aggregate violation tickets based on the rule set's rules. To aggregate policy violations into a violation ticket based on the new logic, activate and run the new rule set. If you only activate but don't run the new rule set, it will run on the next data ingestion in your account.

blocks.text: Every rule set includes a default fallback rule, which provides a default aggregation method for policy violations that don't match any conditions. The fallback rule can be edited, but can't be removed or deleted.

blocks.heading: Configuring Rules in a Default Rule Set

blocks.text: Within a grouping rule set, you can create individual rules that define how policy violations must be aggregated into violation tickets. Every new rule set must include at least one rule in addition to the default fallback rule.
A grouping rule consists of three key components:

blocks.item: If condition: Determines which policy violations the rule applies to.
Then action: Aggregates policy violations into a single violation ticket if they have matching values in all selected fields.
Define Ticket Title By: The title format for violation tickets that are created based on the rule.

blocks.text: To create a grouping rule in a rule set:

blocks.item: In the relevant rule set, click New Rule.
The Create Rule page appears.
See image.
On the Create Rule page:
Name: Enter a name for the rule.
If: Define the rule condition that determines which policy violations must be aggregated into a single violation ticket.
Select a field on which the condition should be based.
Select an operator (Contains, Is Not Empty, Is Empty, Equals).
The available operators vary depending on the field type.
Enter the value to which the rule should apply.
(Optional) Use AND/OR logic to define compound rules.
AND aggregates policy violations only if they meet all conditions.
OR aggregates policy violations if they meet any of the conditions.

Then: Select at least one field from the Group By drop-down menu according to which the policy violations that meet the conditions should be aggregated. All policy violations with the same value are merged into a single violation ticket.
Define Ticket Title By: Select a method to set the violation ticket title.

Smart Text: Use a combination of free text and field names as tokens to set the violation ticket title. For example, you can enter the name of the team based on the business application associated with the violation ticket. To add fields as tokens, enter the field name within double curly brackets. The field's display name automatically translates to the field's system name (e.g., Application Name → application.name).

Expression: Set a violation ticket title using an expression to apply custom value transformations and standardize formats. Supported functions, operators, and references, along with examples, are displayed when clicking the Expression text box.

Click Preview to validate your rule's logic. The preview displays policy violations that match the rule and their relevant fields according to the fields specified in the rule. This can indicate whether the rule's filters apply to the policy violations you intend to group into violation tickets.

If no policy violations match the filter condition displayed in the preview, you might need to adjust the rule's configured filters. Alternatively, a previous rule might be applicable to the relevant policy violations, as grouping is dependent on rule order.
Click Save to add the rule to the rule set.
After adding all the required rules to the rule set, choose an option to save the rule set to complete the process:
Click Save. This saves the rules from the rule set but doesn't reaggregate into violation tickets based on the rule set's rules.
If the rule set is active, the new rule set will take effect either when you click Run or the next time data is processed in the account (e.g., when a data source runs).
If the rule set is inactive, no changes will apply to the grouping of policy violations in the account until the rule set is activated and runs.
From the Save drop-down menu, click Save & Activate to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules to the data in your account.

blocks.text: You can repeat the process to add as many grouping rules as required.

blocks.heading: Order of Rules in a Grouping Rule Set

blocks.text: The rules within a grouping rule set are run sequentially by their order of appearance. A policy violation is aggregated into a violation ticket according to the first rule that applies to it. If no rule applies to the policy violation, it's aggregated by the default fallback rule. You can adjust the order of rules by dragging the rules to your desired order. After rearranging the rule order, click Save to apply your changes.
